question: A dishonest shopkeeper pretends to sell his goods at cost price but uses false weights and gain 10%. How much false weight he is using instead 1 kg weight?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Gain = 10% = 1 ÷ 10.

Ratio of False Weight to True Weight = 10 : (10 + 1) = 10 : 11.

Given True weight = 1 kg = 1000 gm, which corresponds to 11 units.

False weight = (1000 ÷ 11) × 10 = 10000 ÷ 11 ≈ 909.09 gm.

**∴ The correct answer is 909.09 gm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**
